entries.aiSummary: Today's tape shows fragmented catalyst quality with structural red flags: AIOK and NEXR (float <2M) posted morning HODs on legitimate buyback/acquisition news, but BRAI's 96% afternoon HOD arrived on zero-news AU tech with 24M float—a mismatch that suggests late-day retail chase rather than institutional setup. The session split reveals a cold-to-neutral cycle: premarket dominance (OPENZ, SHFS, XXII) with fade percentages 19-24% signals classic pop-and-drop retail exhaustion, while afternoon HOD printing (BRAI, MCRP, AEYE) lacks the catalyst weight or sustained volume concentration this framework demands. Float distribution is bifurcated—sub-2M names (AIOK, NEXR, IPST, FRGT) with real news sit alongside high-float noise (BRAI at 24M, SHFS at 25M on merger tag), and XXII's dilutive offering immediately disqualifies it. This tape favors patient entry on dip-backs into morning-established trends rather than chasing afternoon momentum; AIOK and NEXR merit tape review if pullback flags form, but the NO-NEWS afternoon runners and premarket fade-heavy session indicate conditions are cooling toward late-session exhaustion rather than building institutional accumulation.
